---
title: 'Test without an instance'
status: implemented
description: 'Run a script, an integration or an agent against realistic mock Oore data with @oore/client and MSW, before it touches a real instance.'
---

`@oore/client` ships the same mock data that powers
[demo.oore.build](https://demo.oore.build): two apps, their builds and three
store releases in different states. With [MSW](https://mswjs.io), your code
talks to it as if it were an Oore instance. Nothing is built, uploaded or
released, so a script or an agent can try every call safely.

Open [demo.oore.build](https://demo.oore.build) next to your code to see the
same apps and releases in the web UI.

## Install

```bash
npm install @oore/client msw@2
```

The package is ESM only. Run the examples with Node.js 20 or later: Bun does
not support the request interception that `msw/node` uses.

## Answer every request from the mock

`createOoreMockHandlers` returns MSW handlers that keep their own state. A
project you create shows up in the next list, and a rollout you pause is
paused when you read it again. Timestamps and IDs are fixed, so tests give
the same result every run.

```ts
import { setupServer } from 'msw/node'
import { createOoreClient, listProjects, listReleases } from '@oore/client'
import { createOoreMockHandlers } from '@oore/client/msw/scenarios'

const server = setupServer(...createOoreMockHandlers())
server.listen({ onUnhandledRequest: 'error' })

// Any base URL works: the handlers match every host.
const client = createOoreClient({
  baseUrl: 'https://oore.test',
  token: 'oore_mock_token',
})

const { projects } = await listProjects({ client })
console.log(projects.map((project) => project.name)) // FlutterShop, InternalAdmin

const { releases } = await listReleases({ client })
console.log(releases.map((release) => `${release.store} ${release.state}`))

server.close()
```

`onUnhandledRequest: 'error'` makes a call the scenario does not cover fail
loudly instead of reaching the network.

## What the scenario covers

| Area     | Operations                                                                                                | Data                                                                                                                             |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Apps     | `list_projects`, `create_project`                                                                         | FlutterShop (Android and iOS) and InternalAdmin (Android)                                                                        |
| Releases | `list_releases`, `get_release`, `list_release_events`                                                     | Google Play at 20% and rolling, Google Play halted at 5% after a crash spike, App Store fully rolled out                         |
| Actions  | `raise_release`, `pause_release`, `resume_release`, `halt_release`, `complete_release`, `approve_release` | Each moves the release as the daemon would. An action the state does not allow answers 409 `invalid_release_state`, as Oore does |

Start from other release states with your own list:

```ts
import {
  createOoreMockHandlers,
  defaultOoreScenario,
  haltedReleaseScenario,
} from '@oore/client/msw/scenarios'

const handlers = createOoreMockHandlers({
  ...defaultOoreScenario,
  releases: [haltedReleaseScenario],
})
```

## Mock any other operation

`@oore/client/msw` has a handler factory for every API operation, named after
its operation ID. Use one to answer a call the scenario does not cover, or to
force an error:

```ts
import { HttpResponse } from 'msw'
import { setupServer } from 'msw/node'
import { createBuildMock } from '@oore/client/msw'
import { createOoreMockHandlers } from '@oore/client/msw/scenarios'

const server = setupServer(
  createBuildMock(() =>
    HttpResponse.json(
      { error: 'Pipeline not found', code: 'not_found' },
      { status: 404 },
    ),
  ),
  ...createOoreMockHandlers(),
)
```

Pass each factory the answer you want. The first handler that matches a
request wins, so put overrides before the scenario.

## Test an agent or a CLI script

Tools that are not JavaScript, such as the `oore` CLI, `curl` or an agent,
can point at a small local server that runs the same handlers. Start one with
MSW's `@mswjs/http-middleware` (`npm install @mswjs/http-middleware`), then
set `OORE_URL` to it:

```ts
import { createServer } from '@mswjs/http-middleware'
import { createOoreMockHandlers } from '@oore/client/msw/scenarios'

createServer(...createOoreMockHandlers()).listen(8787)
```

```bash
export OORE_URL='http://127.0.0.1:8787'
export OORE_TOKEN='oore_mock_token'
curl -fsS "$OORE_URL/v1/projects" -H "Authorization: Bearer $OORE_TOKEN"
```

The mock checks no token, and a route the scenario does not cover answers
`404`. Test sign-in failures against a real instance, or with a handler that
answers `401`.
